description: Selected published HAP research with dates, source pointers and explicit limitations. Not a raw workbook or live funding ledger.

funding.title: CDBG — PY2024 reported resources and spending
funding.detail: The published research cites $4,717,936 in CR-15 CDBG expenditures (rounded), a separate reporting measure. The $349,468 program-income component is already included in the resource subtotal and must not be added again.
funding.limit: Resource totals and expenditure measures cannot be treated as an unobligated or currently available balance.

funding.title: CDBG — planned reallocation to housing
funding.detail: A City communication reported a council-approved change moving planned funds from community facilities toward eligible housing activities.
funding.limit: Implementation, amended-plan status, IDIS activity records and actual draws must still be verified. This is not an additional $1.5 million in federal revenue.

funding.title: HOME — PY2024 resources and expenditures
funding.detail: These rounded figures are reported in the project's historical research summary for the PY2024 CAPER. Matching activity commitments, draws and completion records are still needed.
funding.limit: The difference is not proof of free cash, unobligated funds, or assistance available to applicants.

funding.title: HOME — program income carried forward
funding.detail: The draft CAPER reports $534,792.63 received and $7,548.34 applied in its program-income presentation. The arithmetic produces a reported carryforward, not a cash availability test.
funding.limit: Current commitments, draw dates, restrictions and usable balances have not been independently established.

funding.title: HOME — recaptured funds carried forward
funding.detail: The draft separately reports $373,430.46 received and $65,866.33 applied in recaptured funds. These funds are distinct from HOME program income.
funding.limit: No unrestricted rental subsidy or current household eligibility is established by this report.

funding.title: ESG — rapid-rehousing performance
funding.detail: The historical CAPER performance comparison and later-dated ESG grant draw records have different reporting periods and must not be combined into an unsupported cost-per-household figure.
funding.limit: These figures do not establish why reported actual households fell below the target or whether all relevant services were captured.

funding.title: Housing Choice Vouchers — reported funding comparisons
funding.meta: HCV · FY2026 / PY2025 · Tucson and Pima scopes
funding.measure: Different PHA periods and accounting measures
funding.detail: The research question compares an approximately $62.8 million HCV funding narrative with separate payment measures of $49.54 million for Tucson and $9.16 million for Pima County.
funding.limit: Different fiscal periods, PHA jurisdictions, restrictions and accounting categories prevent interpreting the arithmetic as an unspent or available amount.

projects.title: Amazon Flats
projects.detail: The City announced the start of construction in April 2026. An earlier environmental notice proposed 39 project-based vouchers and identified two HOME-designated apartments within the 59 planned apartments.
projects.limit: The City projected fall 2027 completion; a projection is not confirmation of completion, executed contracts, vacancies or current applications. Do not add 59, 39 and 2 as distinct apartment counts.

projects.title: Craycroft Towers and Lee Street Duplexes
projects.detail: City notices describe 74 Craycroft and eight Lee Street apartments. The 82 Section 8 project-based vouchers concern the existing units, with RAD and Section 18 classifications also described for Craycroft.
projects.limit: Not 82 newly constructed units or 82 available vacancies. Executed HAP contracts, occupancy and application procedures remain unverified.

projects.title: Milagro on Oracle
projects.detail: City announcements describe a housing-delivery milestone, crediting El Pueblo Housing Development and Gorman & Company and a combination of new construction and adaptive reuse.
projects.limit: A reported opening is not an independently audited resident count or evidence of currently available apartments.

projects.title: Amazon Motel conversion
projects.detail: A former motel was converted to permanent supportive housing according to City reporting. This is a separate existing-building conversion, not the adjacent Amazon Flats development.
projects.limit: Current vacancies, resident retention and new-referral capacity are not established by a historical completion announcement.

projects.title: Tucson House renovation
projects.detail: The City stated that 25 households would be moving into renovated housing; it also described a broader 358-apartment rehabilitation project. The reported 24-versus-25 figures require clarification.
projects.limit: Renovated units are not newly constructed apartments. A future move statement is not proof that all moves occurred or that external vacancies existed.

questions.title: How is CDBG program income included in reported resources?
questions.detail: $349,468 program income is already part of the $5,418,132 resource subtotal.
questions.limit: Resource arithmetic reproduced from the corrected PR-26; do not count program income twice.

questions.title: Do HOME resources minus expenditures show usable cash?
questions.detail: Rounded historical amounts cannot be interpreted as a live cash balance.
questions.limit: Obligations, draws, eligible-use restrictions and comparable accounting periods.

questions.title: Why do homebuyer outcome counts differ?

questions.limit: Matched reporting definitions, dates and beneficiary cohorts.

questions.title: What explains ESG rapid-rehousing plan versus actual?
questions.detail: The published comparison is 30 planned versus 18 actual households.
questions.limit: Comparable outcome cohorts and any documented agency explanation.

questions.title: Where can the final PY2025 CAPER and its supporting tables be verified?
questions.detail: The City draft references schedules expected in the final report.
questions.limit: Final document, HUD receipt or acceptance and supporting attachments.

questions.title: Was the $1.5 million CDBG transfer new funding?
questions.detail: A planned reallocation changes categories without increasing total CDBG funding.
questions.limit: Amended plan, HUD/IDIS entries, project commitments and actual draws.

questions.title: What still needs explaining in CDBG spending?
questions.detail: The corrected PR-26 reports $4,717,936.37 in formula-CDBG expenditures. The City’s narrative reports $3,433,346.66, leaving a $1,284,589.71 arithmetic difference requiring a transaction-level explanation.
questions.limit: Match formula-CDBG activities and voucher dates to the narrative and corrected PR-26. This is not a finding of missing funds, currently available assistance or a cost per housing outcome. CDBG-CV is reported separately.
questions.source: SRC-023; OMB 2025 Compliance Supplement, PDF p. 61

correction_history.correction: Withdrew the earlier $944,972.60 mixed formula-CDBG/CDBG-CV comparison; retained $1,284,589.71 formula-only arithmetic for transaction reconciliation.

questions.limit: Project IDs, construction and completion dates, and nonduplicative aggregate unit and occupancy counts, with an explanation of how overlaps are removed.

questions.title: How should HCV funding and payments be compared?

questions.title: What do the two Craycroft financing records mean?
questions.detail: Documented: The records appear to concern the same financing. The Arizona Finance Authority lists a $10 million volume-cap allocation, approved February 9 and expiring December 15, 2026. The November 4 Council agenda proposed up to $10 million in project revenue bonds for the same project. They should not be added as separate funding.
questions.limit: Unknown: The adopted action, bond closing and proceeds received remain unverified. Blank closing fields in the older AFA tracker do not establish current status. Next: Check the adopted action, closing documents and use of proceeds.

questions.title: How much CoC funding was requested?
questions.detail: Documented: TPCH submitted a $22,827,346 total FY2026 Continuum of Care request on September 29, 2026. It includes renewals and other categories, not just new funding. The submission is not a final HUD award. [12–13]
questions.limit: Next: Compare final awards with the request. HUD’s November 3 notice says awards are required by December 1, 2026. [14]

questions.title: What is planned for Craycroft and Lee Street?
questions.status: Governing budget and bedroom count unresolved
questions.detail: Documented: The plan is to rehabilitate 82 existing homes: 74 apartments and eight duplex units. El Pueblo Housing Development (EPHD) also describes a Rental Assistance Demonstration conversion, which changes their subsidy structure.
questions.limit: Unknown: Which budget and bedroom count govern? The November presentation lists 124 bedrooms in its summary and 85 in its detailed slide. The summary cost entry is $33.9, without a millions label; the detail gives $34.7 million. Next: Confirm the governing budget and bedroom count, then document public contract status, aggregate occupancy totals and published application and referral rules.

questions.title: What assistance is authorized for El Portal homes?
questions.status: Plan authority documented; contracts and placements unverified
questions.detail: Documented: The October 30, 2026 HCD memo reports that the August 18 PHA plan approval permits project-based vouchers in up to 120 El Portal units during the 2026 plan year. The memo estimates 181 planned voucher units across two phases. The 120-unit statement is attributed to that memo, not independently established here from the August 18 plan. Neither figure establishes placements or an exact unit count for each phase.
questions.limit: Unknown: How many units are covered by signed assistance contracts, and how many households are receiving the new assistance, as of the reporting date? Plan approval does not establish either. The October 30 operating policies were still proposed. Eligibility reviews, inspections and rent determinations are also needed. Next: Obtain aggregate counts of contracted units and households assisted, with reporting dates, inspection-completion totals and effective program policies. Do not request resident names, unit-level addresses or individual case records.

questions.title: What do Housing First’s results tell us?
questions.status: Dated outcomes checked; exclusions and later outcomes open
questions.detail: Documented: Housing First recorded 21 permanent-housing exits among 36 counted leavers (58.3%), after excluding eight of 44 leavers, and all 26 openings filled through Coordinated Entry for July 1, 2025–June 1, 2026. Separately, seven of 43 people in the June 1, 2024–June 1, 2025 permanent-housing exit cohort returned within 12 months (16.3%). These are different groups and periods; weighted scores are not housing-success percentages or evidence of underspending.
questions.limit: Unknown: The aggregate destination categories accounting for the eight excluded exits are not established. Later aggregate outcomes and costs for comparable groups and reporting periods also remain unverified. Next: Obtain an agency-prepared aggregate breakdown by broad destination category and updated outcome totals, with inclusion rules, denominators and reporting periods. Combine or suppress small groups where individuals could be identified; do not request participant records.

questions.title: What explains the project-cost total and unit categories?
questions.status: Cost total and unit categories unresolved
questions.detail: Documented: The November EPHD presentation’s project-cost entries sum to 590.8; its printed total is 593.5. Several entries omit the millions label. Its 1,326-unit total includes projects at different stages and rehabilitation work.
questions.limit: Unknown: The cost unit and total need clarification. The unit total alone does not show how many new homes were completed. Next: Obtain a corrected project table with explicit cost units and separate planned, existing, rehabilitated and completed homes.

The Board cites the amount available for renewals in Tier 1 and says the applicant was notified June 25. This is a submitted funding decision, not a final HUD award. [12, p. 17]
questions.limit: Next: Verify the final award and resulting service capacity. This named record does not identify the unnamed 50% case below.

statements: Documented: HUD’s FY2026 allocation file and Tucson’s FY2027/PY2026 Annual Action Plan agree on four allocations:
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG): $4,962,047 for eligible community-development work, including housing.
HOME: $3,061,840.81 for the Tucson/Pima County consortium.
ESG: $448,998 for Tucson’s Emergency Solutions Grant.
HOPWA: $1,140,597 for housing assistance and services for low-income people with HIV/AIDS and their families.
Together, the allocations total $9,613,482.81. The City separately forecasts $200,000 in CDBG income and $500,000 in HOME income. Each program has its own eligible uses and service area.
Unknown: How much has been received, committed or spent is not established by these allocations and forecasts.

Housing projects and outcomes.question: What do Housing First’s results tell us?
statements: Documented: The FY2026 scorecard reports:

Did people leave for permanent housing? Yes, 21 of 36 leavers included in the calculation, or 58.3%, did. The period is July 1, 2025–June 1, 2026. The scorecard starts with 44 leavers and excludes eight based on their destinations. It does not measure everyone served.
How were openings filled? All 26 recorded openings were filled through Coordinated Entry in the same period. That describes the referral route into those openings, not access for everyone waiting.

Did people return to homelessness? Seven of 43 people who exited to permanent housing in the earlier June 1, 2024–June 1, 2025 period returned within 12 months, or 16.3%. This is a different group and reporting period.

Housing First’s 50/100 and MDOT’s 10/40 are weighted scores, not housing-success percentages. Both programs were exempt from the grant-expenditure measure. Their scores do not establish underspending.

Unknown: The aggregate destination categories accounting for the eight excluded exits are not established. Later aggregate outcomes and costs for comparable groups and reporting periods also remain unverified.

Next: Obtain an agency-prepared aggregate breakdown by broad destination category and updated outcome totals, with inclusion rules, denominators and reporting periods. Combine or suppress small groups where individuals could be identified; do not request participant records.
Source date: TPCH scorecard July 13, 2026; FY2026 methodology pp. 24–26. Exact cells and definitions appear in sources 8–9.

resident_privacy_policy: Resident outcomes are researched through aggregate counts, reporting periods, inclusion rules and denominators. We do not seek resident names, occupied-unit identifiers, tenant rosters or individual case files. Use public or appropriately redacted records and combine or suppress small groups whenever totals or linked information could identify someone. Project and agency identities remain part of public accountability.
